basis: Pituitary hormone deficiencies, cervical spine abnormalities and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; skeletal and hearing abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Localized disorder of buccal mucosa with epithelial intracellular edema.
Congenital humeroradial fusion defines the disease; renal insufficiency is reported without enough frequency evidence to establish involvement in at least 30%.
Neurodevelopmental disease with spastic quadriplegia; dysphagia in 2/4 reflects neurologic motor dysfunction without established gastrointestinal tissue damage.
Primary microangiopathy of dermal vessels causes persistent cutaneous telangiectasias; nonspecific metabolic annotations do not establish metabolic disease.
Congenital cardiac and urinary anomalies; lung hypoplasia in 2/2 and intestinal malrotation in 1/2. Musculoskeletal malformations omitted by cap; cohort is small.
Joubert brain malformation defines the disease; ocular coloboma occurs in 6/11. Renal cysts in 2/11 and nephronophthisis in 1/11 do not establish renal involvement at 30%.
Inherited metabolic neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation; additional organ damage is not established across the subtype umbrella.
Hereditary optic nerve atrophy; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Anthrax infection arises in injection-site skin, subcutis or skeletal muscle.
Localized cutaneous mucinosis producing chronic papules; no systemic endocrine or other organ disease is established.
Non-invasive epithelial neoplasm originating in the exocrine pancreas.
Congenital microphthalmia and blindness with progressive destructive brain atrophy define the syndrome; vomiting alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Lipoprotein metabolism defect; renal dysfunction and hemolytic anemia each occur in 30-79%. Visual impairment occurs in 5-29%; atherosclerosis is separately diagnosed.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the syndrome; diaphragmatic hernia, pectus excavatum and limb malformations occur in 80-99%.
Lens cataract caused by hypocalcemia; the underlying calcium disorder is distinct from this ocular manifestation.
Juvenile or adult form of vanishing white matter leukoencephalopathy, causing cerebral white matter degeneration.
Lymphatic drainage failure causes persistent edema and tissue changes in skin and subcutis; obstruction alone does not establish an immune mechanism.
Tumor originates in breast or rarely prostate, both outside the axes; distant metastases are not common across the umbrella.
Inherited combined lipid metabolism disorder; cardiovascular disease is a separately diagnosed downstream risk.
Skin and esophageal blistering and erosions define the subtype; dental caries and enamel hypoplasia further support gastrointestinal involvement.
Carcinoma originates in major or minor salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Genetically associated immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; intestinal inflammation defines the condition.
Carcinoma in situ confined to the anal canal epithelium.
Herpes simplex infection directly causes inflammation and ulceration of gingiva and oral mucosa.
